question.text: If $y=4 x+3$ is parallel to a tangent to the parabola $y^{2}=12 x$, then its distance from the normal parallel to the given line is

solution.text:
Given equation of parabola is
$$
y^{2}=12 x
$$
On differentiating both sides w.r.t. $x,$ we get
$$
2 y \frac{d y}{d x}=12 \Rightarrow \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{6}{y}
$$
Since, the normal to the curve is parallel to the line $y=4 x+3$
$\therefore$ Slope of normal curve $=$ Slope of line
$\Rightarrow \quad-\frac{Y}{6}=4$
$\Rightarrow \quad y=-24$
From Eq. (i), we get $(-24)^{2}=12 x$
$\Rightarrow \quad 24 \times 24=12 x$
$\Rightarrow \quad x=48$
$\therefore$ Normal point on a curve is (48,-24)
$\therefore$ Distance from (48,-24) to the line $4 x-y+3=0$ is
$\frac{4 \times 48+24+3}{\sqrt{4^{2}+1^{2}}}=\frac{219}{\sqrt{17}}$
